en: Giunta, Paolo. “The Āryadhvajāgrakeyūrā nāma dhāraṇī. Diplomatic Edition of MS Tucci 3.2.16. In: *Sanskrit Texts from Giuseppe Tucci’s Collection*, edited by Francesco Sferra. Rome: Istituto Italiano per l’Africa e l’Oriente, 2008:
187–194. Success! Homage to the Blessed Noble Dhvajāgrakeyūrā!

Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the gods of the Thirty-three on the Pāṇḍukambala stone slab. Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, having been defeated and vanquished by the asuras, approached the Blessed One with great haste and urgency. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he said this to him: "Lord, here I have been defeated and vanquished by Vemacitrin, the lord of the asuras; the gods of the Thirty-three have also been defeated and vanquished. Lord, how should we proceed in this matter? The Blessed One said: "Devendra, take up the Aparājitā [dhāraṇī] called Dhvajāgrakeyūrā, which was previously received by me when I was a bodhisattva from the presence of the Tathāgata Aparājitadhvaja. Having received it, I have proclaimed it in detail to others. Since that time, I do not recall ever experiencing fear, paralysis, or a sign of horripilation, nor even for a single moment a physical pain."
What, O Blessed One, is that dhāraṇī called Dhvajāgrakeyūrā, the invincible?

Namely: *Oṃ jaya 2 vijaya 2 jayavāhini śaṅkari bhayaṅkari prabhañjani rakṣa rakṣa āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajraṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca!* If an adversary or an enemy attacks: *Oṃ jambhaya 2 stambhaya 2 mohaya 2 bhagavati jayavāhini matha matha pramatha pramatha grasa grasa hasa hasa hūṃ hūṃ lambha lambha lambodari trinetre caturvaktre caturdaṃṣṭre caturbhuje asimuśalacakratriśūlavajrakavacamudrādhāriṇi rakṣa rakṣa āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajraṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca bhagavati sarvopadravopasargopāyāsebhyaḥ!* *He he bhagavati hana hana daha daha paca paca matha matha pramatha pramatha dhuna dhuna vidhuna vidhuna hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ bhañja bhañja parasainyaṃ vidhvaṃsaya āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajrasya saparivārasya sarvaśatrūn!* *O Dhvajāgrakeyūrā, tṛṭa tṛṭa tṛṭu tṛṭu ulkādhāriṇi trailokyamathani, destroy the enemy army! Protect, protect Āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajra, his retinue, and all sentient beings from all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions!* *Calā calā cili cili culu culu kala kala kili kili kulu kulu muñca aṭṭaṭṭahāsam! Destroy the enemy army! Terrify them, terrify them! Bewilder them, bewilder them! By the truth of the Buddha, by the truth of the Dharma, by the truth of the Saṅgha, by the truth of those who speak the truth—do not transgress the truth of the Buddha! Do not transgress the truth of the Dharma! Do not transgress the truth of the Saṅgha! Do not transgress the truth of those who speak the truth!* *Lambodari 2, kuṭa kuṭa kuṭṭa kuṭṭa, bring Rudra here! Bring Viṣṇu here! Bring the Moon and Sun here! Bring the Lord of the Three Worlds here! Bring the Lord of All Devas here! Bring all the devas here! Bring all the yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, mahoragas, and nāgas here! Destroy the enemy army!* *Raṅga raṅga raṅgāpaya raṅgāpaya jvala jvala puṣpamālini rundha rundha riṭi riṭi ciṭi ciṭi bhṛkuṭīmukhi parasainyakulomodanakari hala hala hili hili hulu hulu hūṃ hūṃ he he riṇi riṇi riṇamati jambha! O you who are beheld by the Buddhas on the banner, protect, protect Āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajra, his retinue, and all sentient beings, O you who are beheld by all the Tathāgatas, svāhā! Guṇarājaprabhāse svāhā! Sūryārkavimale svāhā! Candrārkavimale svāhā! Sarvagrahanakṣatradhyāmīkaraṇe svāhā! Hūṃ hūṃ rakṣa rakṣa āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajraṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca sarvabhayebhyaḥ svāhā!*

O Lord of Devas, this is that Aparājitā Dhāraṇī named Dhvajāgrakeyūrā. Wherever one may go—in battle, in strife, in conflict, or in dispute—there shall be victory everywhere. Whether bound to the top of a banner or worn around the neck, it should be maintained by a king of men and all heroic persons; it provides protection for them all. Assuming the form of a woman, she stands before them, bestows fearlessness, and provides protection. She puts to flight the enemy army; she is auspicious, pure, and the establisher of glory and fortune.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. With uplifted minds, Śakra, lord of the gods, those monks, and those bodhisattvas rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.

Oṃ! O Blessed One, you who wear armlets upon the tip of your banner; you who destroy the enemy armies and protect your own troops; you whose face is like a meteor! Kha kha! Khāhi khāhi! Strike, strike the enemy army with your infinite mouths and infinite arms! Hūṃ hūṃ! Phaṭ phaṭ svāhā!
The Heart of the Noble Crest-Jewel at the Tip of the Banner is completed.

D612 The Noble Dhāraṇī Entitled “The Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner” (*Ārya-dhvajāgrakeyūra-nāma-dhāraṇī*) In the language of India: *Ārya-dhvajāgrakeyūra-nāma-dhāraṇī* In the language of Tibet: *’phags pa rgyal mtshan gyi rtse mo’i dpung rgyan ces bya ba’i gzungs* Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Thus have I heard at one time: The Blessed One was dwelling among the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three upon a stone slab as white as a crane. At that time, Śakra, the Lord of the Gods, having been defeated and utterly vanquished by the Asuras, approached the Blessed One with a distressed and weary countenance. Having arrived, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and addressed him thus: “Blessed One, while I was engaged in battle with the Asuras, I was defeated and utterly vanquished by the Asura lord Vemacitrin. Since the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three have also been defeated and utterly vanquished, Blessed One, how should we proceed? The Blessed One replied: “Lord of the Gods, you should take up this dhāraṇī called ‘The Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner,’ which is invincible to others. When I was formerly a Bodhisattva, I received this from the Tathāgata Aparājita-dhvaja. Having received it, I explained it extensively to others. I remember that from that time until now, I have never experienced fear, anxiety, or horripilation, nor have I ever suffered physical harm for even a single moment. “Blessed One, what is this dhāraṇī called ‘The Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner’ that is invincible to others? The Blessed One said: *Tadyathā | oṃ jaya jaya vijaya vijaya jayāvahini śaṅkari śaṅkari prabhaṅkari | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca sarvaśatrūn jambhaya jambhaya stambhaya stambhaya mohaya mohaya bhagavati jayāvahini matha matha pramatha pramatha grasa grasa hasa hasa hūṃ hūṃ la hūṃ la hūṃ lamodari | 46a | trinetre caturbakte caturdaṃṣṭre caturbhujai asi-musala-cakra-triśūla-vajrakavaca-dhāraṇi | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvopadravebhyaḥ | oṃ bhagavati hana hana daha daha paca paca matha matha pramatha pramatha dhuna dhuna vidhuna vidhuna hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ bhanydza bhanydza parasainyaṃ vidhvamsaya sarvaśatrūn nāśaya dhvajāgrakeyūre trita trita trita bhrita bhrita ulkā mukhi ulkādhāraṇi trailokyamathani vidhvamsaya parasainyān | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvopadravebhyaḥ cala cala cili cili culu culu kampa kampa kala kala kili kili kulu kulu mundza mundza āṭṭahāsaṃ vidhvamsaya parasainyān | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvopadravebhyaḥ trāsaya trāsaya bhrāmaya bhrāmaya buddhasatyena dharmasatyena saṃghasatyena satyavādināṃ satyena | buddhasatyamatikrama dharmasatyamatikrama saṃghasatyamatikrama satyavādināṃ satyamatikrama | lambodari lambodari kutakuta kuttapaya kuttapaya rudramanāya vaśnimanāya candrasūryabrahmamanāya trailokyādhipatimanāya sarvadevādhipatimanāya sarvayakṣarākṣasagandharvakumbhāṇḍamahoragādhipatimanāya vidhvamsaya parasainyaṃ | raṅga raṅga raṅgapaya raṅgapaya jvala jvala puṣpamālini rundha rundha riti riti citi citi bhriti dhrite bhrikuti mukhaparasenagulotasaḍanikari hala hala hili hili hulu hulu he he rini rini rinimati jambhadhvaje sarvabuddhāvalokite | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvabhayebhyaḥ | sarvatathāgatāvalokite svāhā | guṇarājaprabhāsottame svāhā | sūryārka vimala svāhā | candrārka vimala svāhā | sarvagrahanakṣatradhīmikaraṇi svāhā | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvabhayopadravavyādhyupasargavigrahebhyaḥ svāhā |” “O King of the Gods, by means of this dhāraṇī called ‘The Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner,’ which is invincible to others, whether you are engaged in battle, combat, dispute, or conflict, wherever you go, you shall be fearless and victorious in all things. If it is tied to the top of a victory banner or around the neck, it will protect all kings and heroic men. It will manifest in the form of a woman, stand before one, grant fearlessness, and provide protection. It will increase glory, rout the enemy forces, and cause auspiciousness, purity, fame, splendor, and prosperity to abide everywhere. When the Blessed One had spoken these words, Śakra, the Lord of the Gods, along with the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced and highly praised what the Blessed One had said. The Noble Dhāraṇī Entitled “The Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner” is complete. Translated, edited, and finalized by the Indian preceptors Jinamitra and Dānaśīla, and the chief editor-translator, the monk Ye-shes-sde, with revisions according to the new terminology.

The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner (*Ārya-dhvajāgrakeyūra-nāma-dhāraṇī*) In the language of India: *Ārya-dhvajāgrakeyūra-nāma-dhāraṇī* In the language of Tibet: *’Phags pa rgyal mtshan gyi rtse mo’i dpung rgyan ces bya ba’i gzungs* Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Thus have I heard at one time: The Blessed One was dwelling upon a stone slab as white as a conch shell among the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three. At that time, Śakra, the Lord of the Gods, having been defeated and utterly vanquished by the Asuras, approached the Blessed One with a distressed and trembling countenance. Upon arrival, he prostrated with his head at the feet of the Blessed One and addressed him thus: “Blessed One, while I was engaged in battle with the Asuras, I was defeated and utterly vanquished by Vemacitrin, the Lord of the Asuras. Since the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three have also been defeated and utterly vanquished, Blessed One, what should we do about this? The Blessed One replied: “Lord of the Gods, you must hold fast to this invincible dhāraṇī called ‘The Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner. When I was formerly a Bodhisattva, I received this from the Tathāgata Aparājita-dhvaja. Having received it, I also explained it extensively to others. I remember that from that time until now, I have never experienced fear, anxiety, or horripilation, nor have I ever suffered physical harm for even a single moment. “Blessed One, what is this invincible dhāraṇī called ‘The Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner’? | dhriti dhriti | bhṛkuṭimukhaparasenakulotsādanikari | hala hala | hili hili | hulu hulu | he he | riṇi riṇi | riṇimati | jambhadhvaje | sarvabuddhāvalokite | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvabhayebhyaḥ | sarvatathāgatāvalokite svāhā | guṇarājaprabhāsottame svāhā | sūryārkavimale svāhā | candrārkavimale svāhā | sarvagrahanakṣatradhairyakarane svāhā | rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvabhayopadravavyādhipīḍākalaha-sarvopadravebhyaḥ svāhā!* “By means of this invincible dhāraṇī, ‘The Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner of the King of Gods,’ whether you are engaged in battle, combat, dispute, or conflict, wherever you go, you shall be fearless and victorious in all things. If it is tied to the top of a victory banner or around the neck, it will protect all kings and heroic men. It will manifest in the form of a woman, stand before one, grant fearlessness, and provide protection. It will increase glory, crush enemy armies, and ensure the presence of auspiciousness, purity, renown, splendor, and prosperity. When the Blessed One had spoken these words, Śakra, the Lord of the Gods, along with the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced and highly praised what the Blessed One had said. The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Ornament for the Pinnacle of the Victory Banner is complete. Translated, edited, and finalized by the Indian preceptors Jinamitra and Dānaśīla, and the chief editor-translator Bandé Yeshé Dé, and further revised according to the new linguistic standards.”
